title: QBR - Vertex Labs - Health Check
next_steps: Send updated pricing and TCO spreadsheet
Share SOC 2 and encryption / KMS docs
Run 24h stress benchmark on v2 model and share results
action_items: Jessie Patel: Send pricing + TCO spreadsheet by 2026-08-01
Marco Gomez: Set up Dedicated sizing workshop invite by 2026-08-03
Maya Singh: Provide peak QPS and sequence length distributions by 2026-07-30
Priya Narang: Confirm renewal timeline and internal stakeholders by 2026-08-05
summary: Quarterly health check with Vertex Labs covering usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment. Customer is broadly satisfied but wants clearer cost predictability for Q4 and needs a Dedicated sizing plan for a pilot. Security docs and a benchmark run requested.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-27 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Jessie (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Priya (CSM); Alicia, Tom, Maya (Vertex Labs)

[00:00] Jessie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy to kick off Vertex Labs QBR. Quick agenda — usage review, costs, reliability, and then next steps / pilot planning. Priya will cover support notes.
[00:18] Alicia: Thanks, Jessie. Appreciate you taking the time. We've got Tom and Maya on as well.
[00:24] Tom: Hi all.
[00:28] Marco: Hey team. I'll jump into the performance numbers in a bit.
[00:32] Priya: Quick note — I captured recent incidents and escalations, will surface in reliability section.

[01:10] Jessie: So first, usage — Alicia, high level how has adoption looked this quarter?
[01:18] Alicia: We're seeing steady 12% month-over-month growth on token usage; the fine-tune assistant traffic spiked in May with the new release. Peak hours are around 9am PST, about 1.2k QPS but average around 350 QPS.
[01:36] Maya: Important to call out sequences — average seq len is 480 tokens for the assistant, but some batch jobs hit 2k. Those are the heavy ones.
[01:48] Marco: Got it, that's useful. The 2k sequence jobs will impact cost and KV cache sizing — our runtime prefers shorter sequences for throughput.

[02:10] Jessie: Cost side — we've seen a bump due to those long seq jobs and also some unbatched inference in dev. We recommended batching and prefix caching in May; did you make changes?
[02:22] Alicia: We rolled caching into the assistant, but not universally. There's still some ETL-like batch inference hitting the hosted API unbatched.
[02:31] Tom: We're balancing developer velocity versus engineering time to refactor clients.
[02:38] Jessie: Totally. On the QBR we want to reduce unit TCO — we can send a TCO spreadsheet with estimates for batching, quantization, and Dedicated pricing that models your Q4 forecast.
[02:50] Alicia: That would be helpful.

[03:05] Marco: On the Dedicated side, sizing wise, given 1.2k peak and 2k seq bursts, we'd recommend starting with a 3-GPU pool (A100 equivalent) with burst headroom, or a mixed pool with one high-memory node for the 2k seq. We can put numbers in the sizing workshop.
[03:25] Maya: What about autoscale and burst? We need to ensure latency SLOs during spikes.
[03:31] Marco: Redwood Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling and can be set with burst capacity. There's also policy-based routing — you can route non-critical jobs to cheaper quantized variants.

[03:58] Tom: Latency vs cost — our product team is adamant about sub-200ms 95th for chat. Can you confirm SLA viability on Dedicated?
[04:08] Marco: Sub-200ms 95th depends on model choice and seq length. For short seq chat (<=256) that's achievable; for 480+ tokens it's much harder without more GPUs or sharding. We'll show latency profiles in the workshop.
[04:24] Jessie: Also note caching — prefix/KV caching can drop latency for repeated contexts.

[04:45] Alicia: Reliability — we had two incidents in May: one 40-min region outage and a 15-min elevated error rate. Priya?
[04:54] Priya: The 40-min incident was an upstream cloud routing issue; we routed to fallback region and you lost some requests. We closed the incident with a postmortem and recommended enabling multi-region fallback and stricter timeouts. The 15-min error spike correlated with a model rollout; SE recommended canary rollout which you haven't enabled yet.
[05:14] Maya: We saw duplicated requests during the rollout; that was messy.
[05:19] Marco: Canary rollouts reduce blast radius, plus A/B and automatic fallback policies are in Redwood Console. We'll help you configure canaries and automatic rollback.

[05:45] Alicia: Security/compliance — Tom, the procurement team asked for SOC 2 and KMS integration docs.
[05:52] Tom: Yes, legal needs SOC 2 report, SSO/SAML config, and details about data at rest encryption and customer-managed keys.
[06:02] Jessie: We'll share SOC 2 and KMS docs today; Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and on-prem for air-gapped needs.
[06:10] Alicia: Are audit logs available for dedicated/private?
[06:13] Priya: Yes — per-request audit logs and retention are configurable; we'll include the retention matrix in the doc bundle.

[06:30] Tom: Competitor question — we've heard from infra that Anthropic and Lambda Labs are being considered. How does Redwood stack on cost vs performance?
[06:40] Jessie: The tradeoff is similar; Redwood focuses on production-grade serving with transparent TCO levers — batching, quantization recommendations, and routing policies. We'll include competitor notes in the TCO.

[07:05] Marco: Quick note on model upgrades — you mentioned wanting to move to v2 models next quarter. The main impact will be tokenization differences and memory footprint; we can pre-run a compatibility & perf run in staging.
[07:20] Maya: We need a calibrated benchmark so the product team can sign off.
[07:24] Marco: We'll run the 24h stress benchmark and share logs + token-level latency breakdown.

[07:40] Alicia: On commercial — renewal is in October; any options for reserved commits to reduce unit cost?
[07:48] Jessie: Yes — Dedicated reserved capacity or committed spend gives discounts. We'll model a few commit scenarios in the TCO spreadsheet.

[08:05] Tom: What's the timeline for the Dedicated pilot? We want to start before peak season in November.
[08:12] Jessie: Recommend pilot kickoff in early September: sizing workshop in August, pilot deploy in Sept, run benchmarks and tune in Sept-October. That meets your November readiness.

[08:30] Maya: Who will own the pilot on Redwood side?
[08:33] Jessie: Marco will own the technical side; I'll coordinate commercial and Priya will manage success metrics.

[09:00] Priya: Metrics we'll track: uptime, 95th latency, cost per 1k tokens, cache hit rate, and error rate. We'll put the dashboard template in the console and share the link.
[09:14] Alicia: Great.

[09:28] Jessie: Recap & next steps — I'll send the TCO/pricing + competitor notes, Marco will schedule the Dedicated sizing workshop, Marco will run the 24h perf benchmark on v2 in staging, Maya will send sequence length distributions and peak QPS, Priya will follow up on renewal timeline.
[09:47] Tom: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[09:50] Maya: Thanks.
[09:53] Marco: Thanks, talk soon.

[10:00] End of call.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-heard terms (eg "K V cache" instead of KV cache), and some speaker attribution simplified. Links referenced during call: - TCO spreadsheet (link sent by Jessie) - SOC2 & KMS doc (link to security portal) - Redwood Console dashboard template (link)
